category_title: Low-confidence students requiring constant teacher validation and one-to-one support
scenario_title: Transitioning from manipulatives to drawings for addition
minimal_context: The student is working on a piece of paper with two leaves drawn on it to represent an addition problem about insects and change the math sentence to the standard written form.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Here is a piece of paper with two leaves drawn on it. Please draw the insects on the leaves to solve the addition problem.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Teacher, I am trying to draw the insects on the paper, but it is very hard to draw so many insects. What should I do?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Try writing the math sentence and changing it to the standard written form instead.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I wrote the math sentence. It was very easy to write. Now I am changing it to the standard written form. Is this step right?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Go ahead and compute the numerals in the ones.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Writes the sum wrongly) I computed the ones. I carried this numeral to the tens and put the other numeral at the ones. I checked my answer and it is correct. What do I do next?

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Here is a piece of paper with two leaves drawn on it. Please draw the insects on the leaves to solve the addition problem.

STUDENT: Teacher, I am trying to draw the insects on the paper, but it is very hard to draw so many insects. What should I do?

TUTOR: Try writing the math sentence and changing it to the standard written form instead.

STUDENT: I wrote the math sentence. It was very easy to write. Now I am changing it to the standard written form. Is this step right?

TUTOR: Go ahead and compute the numerals in the ones.

STUDENT: (Writes the sum wrongly) I computed the ones. I carried this numeral to the tens and put the other numeral at the ones. I checked my answer and it is correct. What do I do next?

task.content: Representing an addition problem (insects on leaves) using drawings and changing the math sentence to the standard written form
task.learning_goal: Solve arithmetic problems which involve regrouping

context.materials: Piece of paper with two leaves drawn on it

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When encouraged to draw insects on the paper
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Found it very hard to draw so many insects.

behavior_patterns.condition: In case of addition with regrouping
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Made mistakes after computing the numerals in the ones and writing the sum wrongly. They 'carried' the wrong numeral to the tens and put the other numeral at the ones. They failed to identify the error when they checked their answers.
